notes: per-file times exclude the one-time grammar compile (an untimed warm-up extraction precedes timing)

L1 oracle: universal-ctags 6.2.1 (tier B) over the 316 files fathom reads; the manifest's ctags args map .rake, .ru and Rakefile to its Ruby parser (it reads Rakefile as Rake, which tags tasks only). 101 oracle-only definitions: 58 are the `name=` tag ctags writes beside `name` for every attr_accessor and for attr_writer (the dialect lists `name`, as the source spells it), 18 are alias names ctags cuts at ?, ! or = (`alias has_key? key?` is `has_key`), 6 are constants ctags reads from a comparison (`Array === body`, `RUBY_ENGINE == "jruby"`), and 19 are ctags tagging a local's name for a singleton method or a Class.new local (`def close.callback` is `close`, `def obj.method_missing` is `obj`). 68 dialect-only: 44 attr names on a continuation line more than two lines below the statement ctags reports them at, the 18 alias names above (the other half of the same truncation), and 6 definitions ctags misses (a one-line `module ::HelperOne; def one; '1'; end; end`, `helpers { alias_method :h, :escape_html }`, `define_method(:engine)` in a `Module.new { }` block).

L2 oracle: the grammar's own queries/tags.scm and locals.scm (tree-sitter/tree-sitter-ruby v0.23.1, MIT) run by py-tree-sitter 0.25.2 with tree-sitter-ruby 0.23.1, tier C (D5, calibration/oracles/ts-tags), so L2 is capped at good; the script's tag set equals `tree-sitter tags` 0.26.11's on both subjects (20,073 and 16,825 tags). Its pairs count every constant and every non-local identifier as a call: the dialect takes the method name of each call node and every constant, so its 1,110 missed pairs (of 8,463) are bare identifiers with no receiver (`params`, `settings`, a reader called in its own class), which a syntactic query cannot tell from a local variable read, and its 46 pairs outside the oracle are `super`, which upstream's pattern does not tag. call_recall was .6622 before constants became call targets (and the same dialect held sym_recall .9451, L1 good, before constants, attr_* names, aliases and define_method became definitions).

scip-ruby 0.5.0 (tier A, calibration/oracles/scip-ruby, run on both subjects without a Sorbet config, 0.3 s each) is disclosed, not graded: it resolves a call only where Sorbet can type the receiver, and neither subject carries `# typed:` sigils, so against it the same dialect reads call_recall .5382, call_precision .3869, def_mapping .6139, typed_recall .4488, file_edge_precision .8 (12 of 15 file edges) and file_edge_recall .0124 (12 of 965). The entry's own note (`scip-ruby (Sorbet codebases only)`) says the same; L4 needs a Sorbet-typed subject.

L3: imports.scm (require, require_relative, load and autoload with a literal path and no receiver) and the file-symbol strategy (relative, lib/ and the repo root, .rb) are written and tested (TestResolveFileEdges_RubyRequire, TestFileResolveLangsFromManifests, TestDialectGoldens/ruby imports.rb): 436 imports parse on the two subjects and the resolver's edges span 15 distinct cross-file file pairs (the rest stay inside one file). Ruby names a constant lexically, so a reference to Base inside module Sinatra reaches Sinatra::Base, which the resolver's bare top-level match cannot see: only a class, module or constant defined at the top of its file, or a top-level method, resolves; a nested definition does not. Edges keep the file-resolved label, tier pre-scan.
grammar: tree-sitter/tree-sitter-ruby v0.23.1 (71bd32fb, MIT), unchanged from LB-F1: ruby.wasm.gz 311,992 bytes gzip (1,710,411 raw), 428 peak module pages, 0 faults, 0 ERROR nodes on the 316 files.

changes to the previous ruby dialect (same SourceKinds kept, every symbol it listed still emitted, TestRubyDialectKeepsLegacySymbols): new are RubyConstant (a container, so `Outer::CONST` and the methods of a Struct.new block qualify), RubyProperty (attr_accessor, attr_reader and attr_writer names, qualified `Owner.name`), RubyAlias (`alias` and `alias_method`), RubyMethod for define_method with a literal name, RubyClass and RubyModule for `Name = Class.new` and `Module.new` (and bound to a local), a constant reference as a call target, and .rake, .ru and Rakefile as Ruby. Not emitted, on purpose: a bare identifier as a call, `def obj.x` on a local (no owner to qualify it), `attr :x`, and the assignments ctags does not read either (`A, B = 1, 2`, `X ||= 1`, `A::B = 1`).
disposition: partial: target L3, met L2 (L1 excellent, L2 good) on sinatra/sinatra v4.2.1 and jekyll/jekyll v4.4.1, 316 files: sym_recall .9669, sym_precision .9775, kind_agreement 1, range_agreement .9935, signature_coverage 1 (2,244 callables), call_recall .8688, call_precision .9938 (good: tier C caps L2), 2.21 MB/CPU-s, 0 faults, 428 peak module pages, ruby.wasm.gz 311,992 bytes (unchanged).
